title: Orchestrator metadata fanout lag stalled rollout paths and blocked rollback
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: During a staged canary promotion for model:small-variant@2026-02, the orchestrator's metadata fanout subsystem experienced sustained latency and queueing. This caused per-stage promotion state to diverge between leader and followers, leaving ~7% of traffic pinned to an old variant and preventing automated rollback paths from progressing. The incident degraded latency for a subset of customer requests and triggered multiple failed promotion retries, resulting in higher operational load and a delayed mitigation window.
timeline: 2026-03-01T02:15Z - Alert: rollout health score dropped below 92% for canary-stage-3; oncall alerted via PagerDuty.
2026-03-01T02:27Z - Initial mitigations: paused new canary promotions, disabled automated escalation pipelines.
2026-03-01T02:45Z - Investigation: orchestrator leader reported high metadata fanout latency (median 850ms) and sustained queue depth on fanout workers.
2026-03-01T03:10Z - Attempted manual rollback: controller initiated rollback token but many agents did not ACK due to delayed metadata apply.
2026-03-01T03:33Z - Partial remediation: scaled fanout worker pool x3 and reduced per-fanout backoff window; promotions resumed with manual gating.
2026-03-01T04:20Z - Stabilized: routing converged to intended weights and automated rollback paths were re-enabled with a temporary safety throttle.
root_cause: Primary: Metadata fanout worker pool had an inefficient serialized commit path that amplified slowdowns under bursty rollout traffic, leading to timeouts and partial state application across cluster replicas.
Secondary: Promotion state did not include a versioned checksum in the control plane messages, so followers could not detect partial/older applies and consequently did not trigger failure fencing.
Contributing: Autoscaling thresholds for fanout workers used reactive CPU-only signals; during this event the workers were blocked on I/O and did not scale up fast enough.
mitigations_taken: Paused all in-flight canary promotions and set an emergency global gate to prevent new promotions during investigation.
Scaled fanout worker pool (manual horizontal scale x3) and increased concurrency for apply workers to reduce queue depth.
Temporarily reduced fanout batch size and increased acknowledgement timeout on controller to tolerate longer apply windows.
Executed manual verification sweep to reconcile promotion state across all region leaders and promoted a safe rollback token where required.
long_term_actions: Add versioned checksums to promotion metadata messages and require checksum verification on apply before marking a promotion as successful — owner: Luis Ortega, due: 2026-03-24.
Refactor fanout worker commit path to remove serialized disk sync on hot path; replace with append-only, batched durability with periodic checkpoints — owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-04-07.

Implement pre-flight dry-run for promotions that simulates metadata apply latency under current cluster load and blocks promotions if expected apply p99 > 500ms — owner: Backend Safety Team, due: 2026-03-31.
Enhance autoscaling signals for fanout workers to include queue depth and I/O wait, not just CPU; tune thresholds for faster reactive scale-ups — owner: Infra Reliability, due: 2026-03-21.

Create a rollout-fallback token that enforces fencing: any rollback must be acknowledged by >= 90% of replicas or trigger an operator escalated manual isolation — owner: Runtime Safety, due: 2026-04-14.
Add an observability dashboard with per-stage apply latency, queue depth, and checksum mismatch counts; wire alerting for sustained apply p95 > 300ms — owner: Observability, due: 2026-03-17.

postmortem_notes: The incident surface was larger because the orchestrator lacked a simple detection mechanism for partial applies; adding checksums is low-risk and high-impact.
Manual scaling was effective but not immediate; improving autoscaling signals will reduce future mean time to repair (MTTR).
We observed an operational trade-off between strict durability and rollout latency. The chosen long-term fix favors eventual durability with batched checkpoints to preserve low promotion latency.
Design review with Security and Compliance scheduled to validate checksum approach and any storage changes (KMS/HSM considerations) — meeting 2026-03-12.
review_feedback: PM review (Anika Patel): request to prioritize dashboarding and concise operator actions first to reduce incident blast radius.
Design review (Oliver Grant): suggested adding a visual diff in Console for promotion checksum mismatches before applying rollouts.
SRE review (Haruto Saito): recommended a canary for the batched commit path itself (small internal rollout) before global enablement.
notes: Oncall timeline and Slack threads archived in #incidents/2026-03-01 for post-incident review.
Customer outreach: support sent targeted notifications to 6 affected customers on 2026-03-01 06:00Z; follow-up scheduled after long-term fixes.
Consider making 'promotion apply p95' a first-class SLO metric for Dedicated customers later in 2026 roadmap.
